text:
alexa: Quick sync 1 min  we need a single product-facing roadmap for routing + multi-region + tenant isolation that sales can hand to prospects.

sana: Agreed. Break it into three customer-visible phases (starter, readiness, commercial). Keep gating explicit.

dmitri: Starter = routing primitives (latency/cost/geo), per-tenant hints, and sticky affinity. Should be shipable in ~8 weeks.

keiko: Ops gating for any phase that claims "SLA" must include: telemetry contract, runbook drill, automated fallback SLI, and a successful canary.

marcus: Sales asks to call out what they can promise: e.g., "dedicated lane available with 90d commit" + list of acceptance criteria.

sana: Proposed phases (customer phrasing):
- Starter (0-60d): policy knobs, affinity, minimal telemetry. No commercial SLA.
- Ready (60-180d): tenant lanes, reserved pools, 7d canary, runbook & rollback automation. Eligible for SLA.
- Commercial (>180d): policy DSL, active-active region failover, hardened eviction semantics, jurisdictional controls.

alexa: Can we define launch criteria bullets for Ready? Sales needs crisp checklist.

keiko: Ready launch criteria (draft):
- Canary: 7d live canary with 5-10% traffic across two region pairs
- Perf: p95/p99 tail within 15% of baseline for production models
- Safety: error-rate delta <=0.8% vs baseline across canary tenants
- KV: reconciliation test passes (no divergence after 1 hour post-failover)
- Ops: runbook drill executed and rollback path validated in <10 minutes
- Docs: compatibility matrix for model families published

dmitri: Implementation constraints we must surface: some kernels / quant formats can't run on accelerated lanes. Compatibility matrix is a hard gating artifact.

marcus: Sales top asks (ranked): 1) per-region data residency, 2) private/dedicated pools, 3) p99 tail latency commitments. These map to pricing uplift.

sana: Example policy snippet for customer collateral (short):
```
policy: { id: "regional_pref_v1", priorities: ["residency","latency"], allowed_regions: ["us-west1","eu-west1"], fallback: {type: "global_pool", max_spill: 0.05} }
```
Use it verbatim in the one-pager.

keiko: Telemetry contract minimal events: policy_decision.{tenant,policy_id,reason}, route_selected.{tenant,region,latency_ms}, route_fallback.{tenant,reason}, kv_reconcile.{tenant,status}. Each must include tenant_id & policy_id.

alexa: Pricing model: finance wants compatibility bands (0-3) mapping to uplifts. Can someone produce low/med/high uplift ranges?

marcus: I'll pull finance into the loop. We should present example uplift bands in the collateral: band 2 = +20%-30%, band 3 = +35%-50% (rough). Finance will refine.

dmitri: Technical action: run a 10-working-day spike to produce compatibility matrix + unit-cost delta per band for top 6 model families. Need infra support.

sana: I'll own the spike and the one-pager: deliverables = phases + Ready launch criteria + canary plan + telemetry list + compatibility spike scope. ETA: 10 working days for spike, one-pager in 5 business days.

ops-bot: Canary job scheduled: perf-harness run for eu-us pair at 09:00 UTC tomorrow. Owner: sana.

keiko: Add operational detail: evacuation & soft-eviction flow. Recommend ordering: 1) reduce batch sizes, 2) degrade to lower-cost model family, 3) route to global pool with controlled max_spill. Document thresholds: soft_fraction and hard_fraction.

marcus: Also include a customer FAQ snippet: 3 bullets on overflow behavior, how to request dedicated lanes, and how pricing is calculated. Sales uses this directly.

alexa: One more gating nuance: compatibility matrix must annotate which quantization levels result in how much P99 delta. That determines whether a tenant is eligible for a guaranteed tail latency SLA.

dmitri: Agree. We'll instrument perf-harness to measure p50/p95/p99 delta across quant formats. Spike scope includes that.

sana: Notes captured. Action items: Sana = one-pager + spike owner; Dmitri = run spike and deliver compatibility matrix (10 working days); Keiko = telemetry contract + runbook drill; Marcus = finance uplift sync. Review scheduled next Wed 15:00 UTC.

marcus: Sales note: two prospects said this doc will move procurement. Please prioritize the customer-facing one-pager.

alexa: Thanks all. I'll compile the one-pager draft once Sana posts it and then we can finalize with finance. :thumbsup:
